data.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over ex-CEO Huang's alleged China links
data.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia related to former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

The California Department of Justice said on Thursday it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors. My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information -- and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law," Bonta said in a statement.

 

"Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors." On Tuesday, key House lawmakers said that Huang has voluntarily agreed to appear for transcribed interviews as the company faces intensifying national scrutiny over sales of its advanced computer chips.

Huang will appear before congressional committees on December 1, followed by the company's general counsel, Tim Teter, on December 2.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a message for comment on Thursday.

data.title: Chris Wood hikes exposure to Indian equities as AI trade falters
data.description:
Christopher Wood, global head of equity strategy at Jefferies has hiked exposure to Indian equities in his Asia Pacific ex-Japan relative-return portfolio by one percentage point to 15 per cent, and cut exposure to Taiwan by an equal measure.
 
This is the second time in the last three weeks that Wood has hiked exposure to Indian equities. The development comes on the back of a shap fall in artificial intelligence (AI)-linked stocks globally in the last few weeks.
 
"Financial markets continue to act like the AI capex cycle has peaked in spite of a lack of any compelling evidence as yet of any such development on the ground. GREED & fear will continue to assume for now that the market signal is the correct one where the only issue is whether this is the peak of the cycle or a mid-cycle correction," Wood wrote in his weekly note to investors, GREED & fear. 
ALSO READ: Will inflation, Iran tension spook the market bulls? Jefferies, HSBC answer
 
 
Wall Street fell for a sixth consecutive session, as Anthropic’s strong listing failed to allay concerns over stretched AI valuations and debt-financed technology spending, analysts said.
 
"This could keep global risk appetite weak, although India’s relatively limited exposure to the AI trade may offer a degree of insulation. That advantage, however, is likely to prove selective, with foreign capital increasingly favouring companies backed by earnings visibility rather than broad market exposure," said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a SEBI-registered research analyst firm. 
ALSO READ: AI sell-off hits Indian smallcaps; Sterlite, HFCL down up to 29% in a month
 
Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25 per cent to end at 23,879.20 after gaining as much as 2 per cent earlier in the session. The S&P 500 lost 2.02 per cent to close at 7,175.83 levels. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), on the other hand, skidded 2.19 per cent, or 1,101.11 points, to close at 49,097.06. The last time the index closed below 50,000 was in June, data shows.
 
Tough test
 
After a nearly 15 per cent rebound from recent lows, Indian equities, analysts believe, face a tougher test as the global backdrop turns increasingly adverse. The market’s ability to attract buyers amid renewed selling pressure, they suggest, will be critical in determining whether the rally can extend or begins to lose momentum.
 
On the downside, 25,400 forms the immediate support zone, followed by 25,300, said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. "Holding above 25,400 will be crucial to sustaining the prevailing bullish momentum. The near-term outlook remains bullish, although elevated momentum levels warrant caution against aggressive buying at higher levels," he added. 
ALSO READ: Nvidia stock falls 32% in Nov: Is it a buying opportunity? Analysts answer
 
On the downside, 25,400 (Nifty) / 82,700 (Sensex) and 25,320/82,500 would act as key support zones, while 25,650/83,500 and 25,700/83,700 could act as crucial resistance levels for the bulls, according to Shrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research at Kotak Secutities. 
 
"However, a break below 25,200/82,200 could weaken the structure and drag the indices back towards the 25,100–25,000/81,900–81,600 support zone. The strategy should be to buy select stocks between the 25,400 and 25,200 levels,” he added.

data.title: Delhi's AQI improves to 269, Gurugram's air remains most polluted in NCR
data.description:
Delhi’s air quality improved slightly on Friday, with the city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) falling to 269 at 8 am, placing it in the ‘poor’ category, according to real-time data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). PM2.5 remained the prominent pollutant.
 
The improvement was reflected across the capital’s monitoring network. Of the 59 monitoring stations, 57 reported valid readings, of which 53 recorded AQI levels above 200, while 14 were in the ‘very poor’ category, with readings above 300. None reported ‘severe’ air quality.
 
Under the CPCB's National Air Quality Index classification, readings between 0 and 50 are categorised as ‘good’, 51 and 100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 as ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 as ‘poor’, 301 and 400 as ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 as ‘severe’.
 
 
Sirifort recorded the highest station-level AQI at 348, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) at 336, Pusa (IITM) at 335, Burari Crossing at 333 and Chandni Chowk at 330. NSUT Jaffarpur recorded 329, while ITO stood at 321, Ghoga at 321, Delhi Technological University (DTU) at 319 and Talkatora Garden at 316.
 
Meanwhile, Lodhi Road recorded the lowest AQI at 162, followed by IMD Lodhi Road at 173. Both were in the ‘moderate’ category. NSIT Dwarka recorded 193, while Cantonment Area stood at 195.
 
Air quality across the National Capital Region (NCR) remained largely in the ‘poor’ category. Gurugram recorded the highest AQI among the neighbouring cities at 291, followed by Greater Noida at 236 and Noida at 226. Faridabad recorded an AQI of 165, placing it in the ‘moderate’ category.
 
Stage I and II measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (Grap) remain in force across Delhi-NCR. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has also retained separate restrictions on dust-generating demolition and outdoor construction activities, along with directions on physical office attendance, under its October 30 order. These measures are scheduled to remain in force until November 20.

data.title: Apple plans AI agent that can browse web, control apps and write code
data.description:
By Mark Gurman
 
Apple Inc. is developing its own autonomous artificial intelligence agent that can get things done on behalf of users, looking to enter a fast-growing market already being pursued by OpenAI, Anthropic PBC, Meta Platforms Inc. and others. 
The company outlined the plans in job listings added to its website this week. In one, Apple said it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.
 
The move follows the breakout success of Meta’s Muse, which has captured the attention of consumers in recent months with its ability to make restaurant reservations, book travel and prepare news briefings. There’s also been a proliferation of tools that let AI control Mac computers and program software. 
 
 
Shares of Meta and Anthropic slid in late trading after Bloomberg News reported on Apple’s efforts. Meta fell nearly 2 per cent, while Anthropic dropped more than 3 per cent. 
 
Anthropic PBC recently widened user testing of its own agent, called Duet, while OpenAI has expanded the capabilities of Dots. And Alphabet Inc.’s Google overhauled its agent, now called Tasks, earlier this week. Like Elon Musk’s Grok Bot, Tasks lets the system make phone calls on a user’s behalf — in addition to offering standard AI agent features. 
Apple’s App Store has been dominated by AI agents, with Muse long occupying the No. 2 spot among free apps, just behind TikTok, on Thursday. OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude were also both in the top five.
 
OpenAI, Anthropic and Musk’s SpaceXSI are also behind popular developer coding tools Codex, Claude Code and Cursor.
 
Bloomberg News reported earlier this month that Apple was developing its own AI agent offering, but the new job listings offer fresh evidence of the company’s plans. Apple has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year, but development remains in the early stages. An Apple spokesperson didn’t respond to a request for comment.
 
“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the job listing reads. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.”
 
The listing says the company has a team building the “foundation for that future” and that Apple is looking for the hired manager to “make it real.” John Ternus, the tech giant’s new chief executive officer, has been pushing software engineering chief Craig Federighi to move faster and take a bolder approach to AI — with an agent being key to that effort.
 
“People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service. We’re building AI agents that can do the same,” the listing says. The posting adds that Apple is working on agents that can “plan and carry out multistep tasks” across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and application programming interfaces, and they can “coordinate specialized subagents along the way.”
 
The company strongly indicates its platform would be capable of autonomously navigating the interfaces of its operating systems. The listing specifically mentions development of “general-purpose computer-use agents,” the technology that allows ChatGPT and Muse to control a Mac. Google Gemini added such functionality earlier on Thursday.
 
Another central component is privacy, with Apple saying that safety needs to be built into the system’s design. “Agents that can run code, use credentials, and act on a user’s behalf need strong permission models, sandboxing and transparency.”
 
Sandboxing refers to a process that lets engineers test software without the risk of it breaking out into external networks, the rest of the operating system or the broader internet. 
 
As the company develops its own agent, Apple is also making it more difficult for competing bots to gain broad control over its computers. In the beta version of the forthcoming macOS 27.3 operating system, the company has introduced new warning screens that prompt users to reconsider granting third-party agents permission to control their Macs.
 
With the change in 27.3, ChatGPT users now need to engage in 14 distinct steps to enable support for third-party computer-use tools, up from four. While Apple has positioned the shift as a move to protect customers, some AI companies and users see it as an attempt to slow down the competition. 
 
Apple has already been sued by the US Justice Department for actions such as blocking third-party access to features and hardware.
 
While Apple is still far from introducing its own full-fledged AI agent, it has taken steps to integrate its Siri digital assistant more deeply into third-party apps. The company’s upcoming iOS 27.3 release lays the groundwork for deeper collaboration between Siri AI and outside applications, allowing the assistant to, say, book a car or restaurant reservation.
 
Still, the updated system doesn’t go as far as a full-fledged agent, which can autonomously carry out complex tasks across multiple apps and services in the background with little additional instruction from the user.

data.title: US approved AI chip sales for China firms, including Tencent, Alibaba: Data
data.description:
By Maggie Eastland and Brody Ford
 
Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. received US Commerce Department approval earlier this year to ship hundreds of thousands of AI chips to Chinese customers, including some companies that were later added to a Pentagon list of businesses accused of aiding China’s military, according to new documents. 
As of May, the US had granted permission to buy a total of 272,000 older-generation AI processors to Chinese tech giants Tencent Holdings Ltd., Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and Baidu Inc., along with electric-vehicle maker BYD Co., licensing data released on Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs House Committee show.
 
 
The Pentagon had briefly added Alibaba, Baidu and BYD to its roster of military companies in February, before the list was withdrawn. Those names were included in a June update of the list, meaning they hadn’t been formally blacklisted at the time Commerce officials approved the licenses. Tencent, however — which received US permission to buy 150,000 chips — was put on the Pentagon’s so-called 1260H list in January 2025.
 
The House panel’s disclosures offer more ammunition to policymakers in Washington who want an even tougher crackdown on AI chip exports to China. Nvidia and AMD, two of the most valuable US companies, are already largely locked out of the potentially biggest market to their products. They’ve lobbied, unsuccessfully, for freedom to ship AI-related hardware to the Asian nation, arguing it actually helps US national security.
 
The findings promise to intensify congressional scrutiny of the Commerce Department and its Bureau of Industry and Security, which is responsible for US export restrictions on sensitive technology including AI chips. The head of BIS, Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler, has come under increased pressure from lawmakers for answers about whether Nvidia intervened in a smuggling investigation. 
 
House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast released the data a week after Jensen Huang’s ouster as Nvidia chief executive officer, an episode that put a spotlight on whether the chipmaker and the Trump administration had done enough to abide by US export curbs aimed at keeping advanced American technology out of China.
 
Mast’s committee has asked Kessler to appear in early December for a hearing on the matter, though the BIS chief so far has not yet publicly agreed to appear. On Dec. 1, Huang is scheduled to deliver a closed-door briefing to three House national security committees, while Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to brief the Senate Banking panel, though a date has not yet been finalised.
 
An Nvidia spokesperson said that the review and licensing process spanned more than half a year, with approvals subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. In a statement, an AMD spokesperson said the company “complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations.”
 
Spokespeople for BIS didn’t respond to a request for comment. 
 
The licensing data show that US AI chip designers were keen to gain a foothold in the Chinese market. That’s set to become even harder under a new rule announced by Commerce this week aimed at blocking Chinese companies from overseas access to AI processors.  
 
Export license applications had piled up after President Donald Trump agreed in late 2025 to let Nvidia export its older-generation H200 AI processors to approved Chinese buyers — a decision that came after intense lobbying by Huang. As part of the agreement, AMD was allowed to sell its Instinct MI325X chips.
 
Overall, Nvidia and AMD requested to export 3.4 million AI chips to China, data posted by the committee show. Mast’s panel has oversight of BIS and received the information directly from the administration.
 
BIS ultimately approved far fewer shipments to Chinese customers than were requested, allowing sales of nearly 880,000 AI chips. Chinese tech conglomerate Alibaba received a small share of the chips its desired, securing approval for 75,000 AI chip sales out of about 950,000 requested, according to the data. Tencent, Baidu, and BYD each saw their full requests approved. 
 
The document released by the House committee didn’t specify which chips the approved Chinese firms had applied to acquire. 
 
In the three months that ended in October, Nvidia booked $2.4 billion in revenue from H200 sales to China, or about 2.2 per cent of data center revenue. In the prior quarter, when China first allowed sales, it totaled less than 1 per cent of total data center revenue. Nvidia has since stopped all H200 shipments to China, even those approved by the US government, its interim CEO Colette Kress told investors during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday.
 
A BIS rule published in January gave BIS the ability to approve sales of both those processors on a case by case basis, subject to various conditions, including that the US would receive a 25 per cent cut of any revenue. The H200 is part of Nvidia’s Hopper class of chips, now two generations behind its new Vera Rubin line.

data.title: US lawmakers near deal to ban Chinese cars, target bill by year-end
data.description:
By Josh Wingrove, Gabrielle Coppola, David Welch and Steven T. Dennis
 
Lawmakers in Washington are closing in on a deal to ban Chinese cars from the US, according to people familiar with the matter, following last-minute negotiations aimed in part at sparing Mercedes-Benz Group AG, which is nearly 20 per cent owned by Chinese entities. 
Republicans and Democrats from auto-producing states behind the effort aim to send a bill to President Donald Trump’s desk by the end of the year, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the deliberations are private. If enacted, the profitable US car market would be walled off to automakers such as BYD Co. and Geely Automobile Holdings Inc., whose low-cost, technology-packed electric vehicles have rapidly gained market share in Europe and South America.
 
 
Chinese cars are effectively shut out of the US because of steep tariffs and restrictions on Chinese vehicle technology imposed by the Commerce Department. Enshrining a ban into law would take those measures a step further to address growing concerns about national and economic security threats posed by China’s ambition to dominate the global auto industry.
 
Details about the measure are still being hammered out. Republican Senator Bernie Moreno on Wednesday briefed automaker representatives on changes under consideration to earlier legislation that aimed to block Chinese connected vehicles from the US, including provisions that would shield Mercedes from an outright ban, said the people.
 
Automaker representatives were broadly supportive of the effort Moreno described, though a Mercedes official voiced reservations and negotiations remain underway, the people said. Proponents are working to pass the measure before the next Congress begins in January, the people said.
 
“We continue to meet with all stakeholders who have a shared interest in ensuring this important legislation becomes law in this Congress,” Mercedes said in a statement.
 
A bill advanced by a Senate panel earlier this year would have prohibited manufacturers that are more than 15 per cent owned by Chinese entities from selling cars equipped with technology that can transmit data. Mercedes, which has lobbied for changes to that bill, is nearly 10 per cent owned by China’s BAIC Motor Corp., a state-owned carmaker.
 
Li Shu Fu, the billionaire founder of Chinese carmaker Geely, also holds nearly 10 per cent of Mercedes’ shares, putting the company above the earlier bill’s 15 per cent threshold.
 
Lawmakers are in talks with multiple parties, including Mercedes, and have expressed optimism that an agreement could be reached as early as this week, said one person close to the talks who asked not to be identified. Provisions under discussion include looser rules for companies with passive ownership stakes that lack voting power and how such an approach would be structured and verified.
 
The White House did not respond to requests for comment.
 
Republican Senator Katie Britt of Alabama, a major hub of Mercedes’ sport utility vehicle production, said she has worked through the bill with Moreno and believes both Mercedes and Alabama will be protected.
 
“We understand that there will be some adjustments that have to be made, but feel good about Mercedes continuing to be able to thrive in our state and across the country,” she said.
 
Banning Chinese cars would also run counter to a more permissive approach taken by Europe and Canada. Chinese automakers have quickly made inroads in Europe, in particular, leading to intense competition with homegrown brands. The EU has started to pull back after Chinese automakers rapidly expanded their share of the market there, reaching an agreement last month with China to curb imports of hybrid vehicles into the bloc.

data.title: Iran war costs surpass $48.3 billion; Pentagon yet to assess base damage
data.description:
The costs of the Iran war have risen to an estimated $48.3 billion as of November 13, but because that total does not include damage to US bases attacked in West Asia, lawmakers are pushing for the Pentagon to provide those figures.

Arthur Miller, a Pentagon budget official, provided the latest overall cost estimate on Thursday to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which is considering his nomination to be Navy comptroller. The $48 billion figure includes the costs of military operations, as well as for replacing equipment and munitions.

Democratic Sen Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut pressed Miller for an estimate on damage to US installations, which Miller said he didn't have. Republican Sen Roger Wicker of Mississippi, the committee's chair, directed Miller to try to provide an answer as soon as possible.

 

An Associated Press analysis found that Iran attacked aircraft hangars, systems that detect incoming strikes, warehouses, troop housing and more, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage.

The war's price tag has been a flashpoint in Congress, with debates over costs intensifying as the Trump administration asks lawmakers to pass a $1.5 trillion defense budget. After the unpopular war and its economic effects contributed to severe Republican losses in the midterm elections, financial battles over the conflict will only escalate once Democrats take control of Congress in January for the remainder of President Donald Trump's term.

The Pentagon has faced growing calls from Democrats to release estimates on the damage Iran has done to American bases in the Middle East through missile and drone attacks.

Sen Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, grilled acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao on the costs of the war at his confirmation hearing on Tuesday for the permanent job.

Citing independent estimates and media reports, Warren said the US naval blockade on Iranian shipping costs about $32.5 million a day, while an Iranian attack on the Navy's regional headquarters in Bahrain did at least $400 million in damage.

Cao confirmed the figure for the blockade but said he could not offer a full damage assessment in Bahrain because "it's a nonpermissive area for us to go". Cao told a reporter months ago that Iran "blew the hell out of Bahrain".

data.title: Musk distances from MAGA after Republican losses; Trump calls him a friend
data.description:
Elon Musk was in the front row at Donald Trump's second inauguration and has spent hundreds of millions of dollars trying to help the Republican president and his "Make America Great Again" allies win elections.

Now, after Republicans' midterm thrashing by Democrats, the world's richest man insists he's not a MAGA acolyte after all and feels "pretty foolish" for spending so much money on the cause.

It's the latest example of billionaire tech executives shifting their stances as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and many more US statehouses in January after they spent months promising a regulatory and oversight crackdown on artificial intelligence firms, their data centre expansion and their interactions with the Trump administration.

 

"I mean, I'm not MAGA," Musk told The New York Times on Wednesday during the newspaper's DealBook Summit.

"I'm not sure what MAGA means," added the Tesla and SpaceX CEO, who once sported a black MAGA hat in the Oval Office and coined the "Dark MAGA" label. "But I, I don't think I'm, like, if, if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party," Musk continued, "then I certainly don't have that. I think there are, there, there are positives and negatives in both parties." Trump takes Musk's shift in stride Trump, whose relationship with Musk has ranged from ally and trusted adviser to pariah, reacted Thursday with a seeming shrug.

"He's a friend of mine," Trump told NBC News in a telephone interview, similar to how the president described Russian President Vladimir Putin when they met earlier in the day in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen. "Elon is -- Elon's got very good intentions. I mean, he was with me the whole -- he travelled with me." Musk, who has based himself and several of his companies in Texas, spent more than $400 million on Trump-aligned Republicans running in November. That included around $200 million backing Texas Senate nominee Ken Paxton, who lost to Democrat James Talarico.

Democrats scored sweeping victories after making Musk, other tech titans and the proliferation of artificial intelligence and AI data centres a campaign focus. They plan new scrutiny on the industry, including congressional investigations into tech firms' dealings with Trump and his administration. That leaves Musk and others scrambling to rebrand themselves after spending years aligning closely with Trump and his fellow Republicans as they sought government contracts and favourable policies on everything from taxation to AI regulation.

Palantir co-founder and CEO Alex Karp, whose AI software company counts the Pentagon among its lucrative government clients, earlier this month raised eyebrows when he insisted to Politico that he's always been a progressive.

"I've been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far-left environment," he said. "I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir -- all of our products are essentially progressive." Karp, a donor to Trump's White House ballroom project who has adopted the president's rhetoric to describe his own business as "anti-woke," said he's willing to support a Democrat for president in 2028.

At the Times' event, Musk said if he had a do-over, he "probably" would have "spent less money" on the midterms.

"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," Musk told columnist Andrew Sorkin. "Or maybe it would've been much worse without that. But it certainly shows that American elections are not just about money." Democrats and Trump offer takes on Musk's future Musk sat alongside other Big Tech billionaires at Trump's inauguration and led the president's Department of Government Efficiency, a post that for months made him the most high-profile figure in the administration other than Trump himself.

Hours after Trump was sworn in on Jan. 20, 2025, Musk appeared at a Trump rally in Washington, where he enthusiastically embraced the president's agenda and his supporters.

"This was no ordinary victory," he said. "This was a fork in the road of human civilisation. OK? There are elections that come and go. Some elections are important, some are not. But this one really mattered. ... It is thanks to you that the future of civilisation is assured." Some Democrats were unimpressed with Musk's change in tenor.

Responding to Musk's turnabout on X, the social media platform that Musk owns, Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona was concise: "You are still getting a subpoena." Trump, his friendly remarks notwithstanding, offered his own prediction about Musk's future.

"MAGA, to me, means something very specific," the president said, without elaborating, "and when people veer from it, they don't do very well.

data.title: Russia open to Nato-like security guarantees for Ukraine: US envoy
data.description:
US envoy Jared Kushner on Thursday said Russia is "comfortable" with Nato-like security guarantees for Ukraine to end the war as it nears the five-year mark.

Another American envoy, Steve Witkoff, said US President Donald Trump discussed Ukraine and a peaceful end to the war during his trilateral talks with the Russian and Chinese leaders earlier Thursday.

Kushner and Witkoff met with European allies in Berlin to discuss their support for Ukraine after a third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday, after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.

 

Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between Kushner, Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Trump's direct talks with Putin.

The American leader called into the Berlin talks following his meeting with Putin, Kushner said.

Putin acknowledges the damage and vows to strike back "We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that," Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China.

He insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware or ammunition.

Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been "seriously damaged" but vowed to rebuild it.

The rail section is believed to be stronger than the road side, to bear the greater weight of cargo wagons.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support front-line troops. It is a potent reminder of Russia's illegal annexation of the territory and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Zelenskyy, and the train track was damaged by domestically produced Neptune missiles, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said.

Now Russia will need to reroute fuel and ammunition supplies over land, where "our drones are waiting for the cargo," the ministry said.

Attacks kill 4 civilians in Russia, 2 in Ukraine, officials say The Russian Defence Ministry said Thursday that its air defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.

A Ukrainian attack on Russia's Saratov region killed three people and wounded two others, local Gov. Roman Busargin said, and a drone killed a woman travelling by bicycle with her 8-year-old grandson in the Bryansk region, Gov. Egor Kovalchuk said.

Ukrainian authorities said that Russia launched anti-ship missiles and 98 drones at Ukraine, with hits recorded at 18 locations. Explosions and sirens rang out across Kyiv during the day, and the Dutch and Austrian embassies sustained minor damage, officials said.

Two people, including a 44-year-old woman, were killed and at least 23 people, including a 12-year-old boy, were reported wounded as Russian strikes caused damage in 12 regions.

Russia's bigger army hopes to exhaust Ukraine on the front line through sheer weight of numbers in terms of soldiers, armor and weapons. But Kyiv's defences are largely holding the Russians back, sapping Russian momentum with the help of drones that quickly choke off troop advances.

Russia has resorted to strategic bombing to wear down Ukraine's resistance, placing special emphasis on knocking out power ahead of winter, while Kyiv's domestically developed long-range drones and missiles have struck deep inside Russia, often targeting its oil refineries.

Kyiv fears Trump and Putin may try to decide Ukraine's fate In China, Trump called Putin "my friend." The American president's relationship with Zelenskyy, meanwhile, has soured.

European leaders have tried to isolate Putin diplomatically and have heavily sanctioned the Russian economy.

Ukrainian officials fear their country's fate could be determined by agreements between Trump and Putin, while European governments are alarmed by Moscow's aggression.

The question of US support for Ukraine, severely curtailed under Trump, could be raised by Democrats in Congress after their wins in the midterm elections.

Britain's Prince Harry offered a veiled criticism of the US government's policy toward Ukraine, saying in an interview released late Wednesday that he believes there is a "big separation" between the Trump administration's stance and that of the American people.

Merz, Macron and Burnham to meet with US envoys and Zelenskyy Kushner and Witkoff have led Trump administration efforts to end nearly five years of war following Russia's all-out invasion of its neighbour and recently have mediated new discussions, though the talks have yielded no major breakthrough.

Kushner said Thursday on X that Washington's priority at Thursday's meeting in Berlin is to "further strengthen our close coordination with Ukraine and Europe, work toward a unified position on the key elements of a lasting peace, and to jointly prepare the agenda and proposed format for the next round of multilateral negotiations." The meeting will also explore how Ukraine's European backers can fit into postwar security arrangements. Kyiv wants to ensure that Russia doesn't invade again, while Moscow wants to keep the Nato military alliance away from its borders.

Putin said in Shenzhen that the Kremlin is not against European participation in talks, but "we need to understand with what Europe will come to these negotiations." The Kremlin has proposed to European officials through diplomatic channels to come to Moscow "to determine their position," Putin said, without elaborating.

No date has been set for the next round of talks, he said.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to say which European officials had been invited or whether Moscow had received a response, Russian state news agency Tass reported.
